bio.breve: Isabella Pistillo was born in 1969 in Puglia, southern Italy. She paints in acrylic on canvas, with brush and palette knife, in her studio on via Felice Orsini in Andria. Her work centers on the female face and figure, seen through Cubism and twentieth-century painting. Her paintings hang in homes in Italy and abroad, as far as New York.
lunga: I was born in 1969 in Puglia, and this is where I still paint. My studio is on via Felice Orsini, in Andria: every painting on this site was made there.
For me, painting is a game. It's my first thought in the morning and my last before I fall asleep.

I almost always paint women. Faces seen from the front and in profile at the same moment, bodies made of black lines and solid color: red, ochre, emerald green, midnight blue, sometimes gold. I owe a lot to Cubism and the painters of the twentieth century: they taught me that a face can be taken apart and put back together and still be recognizable.
I work in acrylic on canvas. I use the brush for drawing and the palette knife for texture, which I want you to see and almost touch.
Besides paintings I've worked on prints, on fabric and on clothing, and I've collaborated with [architecture studios / projects to name]. [Training, main exhibitions, awards: to fill in.]
My paintings hang in homes in Italy and abroad. One was shipped to New York.
bio.citazione: People have to fall in love.
bio.dato_tecnica: Acrylic on canvas, brush and palette knife
bio.foto_didascalia: Isabella in her studio on via Felice Orsini. Photo: [photographer], 2026.

paragrafi: I almost always paint women's faces, and almost never from a single point of view. In the same face I put an eye seen from the front and a nose seen in profile.

I learned this by looking at the Cubists and twentieth-century painting. I take the face apart and rebuild it with a few black lines and solid color. [Isabella: are the faces real people or imagined? Add a sentence.]

The painting is born in the mind first. By the time I reach the canvas I already know where the gaze goes, where the red goes, where the background stays empty. Then with the palette knife I spread and scrape the paint, and sometimes the painting changes course. That's why I say painting is a game.
Some colors come back from one painting to the next: cadmium red, ochre, emerald green, deep teal, the black of the outlines. Often there's a touch of gold.

atelier.intro: Every painting goes through the same five stages, in the same studio on via Felice Orsini, in Andria. It takes days, sometimes weeks.

passi.testo: I stand in front of the blank canvas, I stare at it, I study it. First I prime it with a very watery acrylic wash, softened with white: it lifts the sheen off the canvas and helps the color grip.
The painting is already complete in my mind. I bring it onto the canvas with the drawing: the lines of the face, the profile, where the hands go. Without the drawing I add nothing.
Then comes color, in solid fields: red, ochre, green, midnight blue, the black of the outlines. Layer after layer, until background and figure hold each other up.
With the knife I spread and scrape the paint. It leaves marks a brush doesn't, and the surface gains relief: in raking light you can see the ridges of paint.
When there's nothing left to take away, I sign, bottom right, by hand. Then the painting is photographed whole, in two close-ups and at the signature: those are the images on its page.

commissioni.sottotitolo: A painting made for your wall.
commissioni.intro: Sometimes the right painting doesn't exist yet. So I paint it. We start with a conversation about the room, the light and who lives there; the rest we decide together on the sketch.

fasi.testo: You write me a few lines, then we talk on the phone, on a video call or in the studio in Andria. You tell me about the house, the light, the colors you already have.
I ask a few questions and a photo of the wall. I also like to know who will look at the painting every day.
I send you a sketch with the size and colors. We talk about it and adjust it together if needed. I only start painting once you're convinced.
20 to 30 days, depending on the size. If you like, I'll send you a few photos as it grows.
The signed painting leaves the studio packed by hand and insured. To Italy, to Europe or further away.

rag.testo: 100% cotton, 308 gsm, matte and velvety. Soft colour and no glare: the museum paper for colour photography.

baryta.testo: Cotton with a baryta layer, 315 gsm, glossy. Deep blacks and full reds: the look of a silver gelatin print.

washi.testo: Japanese paper made from kozo (mulberry) fibre. The texture shows and light sits inside the paper.

bizan.testo: Washi handmade in Japan, 200 gsm, four deckled edges. It only exists in sheets up to A1, so we use it for editions up to 45 × 60 cm.

alu.nota: Slim profile, cotton mat, UV glass
alu.testo: 15 mm profile, as in galleries. Cotton mat, UV-filtering glass.

oak.nota: Solid wood, the print floats inside
oak.testo: Solid natural oak. The print is mounted on a panel and floats with 15 mm of air around it: no glass.

walnut.nota: Solid walnut, Tru Vue Museum Glass
walnut.testo: Solid walnut, cotton mat, Japanese paper hinges. Museum Glass: under 1% reflection and 99% of UV blocked.
